title: Foxconn now makes more money from AI servers than from everything else combined
excerpt: Foxconn cloud and networking revenue hit 51% in Q2, passing half for the first time. Net profit rose 35% to a record.
content_html:
Foxconn crossed a line this quarter that it will not cross back. Its cloud and networking division, the one that builds AI servers, made up 51% of revenue in the three months to June.

That is the first time the segment has passed half. Smart consumer electronics, the division that contains the iPhone, came to 29%.

The profits followed. Net profit reached NT$59.97bn, about $1.86bn, up 35% on a year earlier and the company’s highest ever for a second quarter.

The quarter in numbers

Consolidated sales hit NT$2.53 trillion, up 41% year on year and 19% on the previous quarter. Analyst forecasts were beaten on both profit and revenue.

The cloud and networking share climbed fast. It was 48% in the first quarter, with computing at 15% and electronic components at 5%, per Taiwan’s Central News Agency.

Earnings per share came in at NT$4.27, against NT$3.19 a year earlier. First-half profit reached NT$109.89bn, up 27%.

July was bigger still. Revenue that month jumped 54.2% to a record NT$946.5bn, Bloomberg reported.

What the company is promising

Rotating chief executive Michael Chiang framed the shift as structural rather than cyclical. Cloud investment, he told analysts, “will become the most critical growth driver for Hon Hai over the next few years”.

He drew a distinction that matters for a contract manufacturer. AI infrastructure demand is steady, unlike consumer electronics, which lives and dies by seasonal cycles.

He also argued the buildout has barely started. Cloud providers and AI labs are the big buyers so far, while government and corporate adoption remains, in his words, in its infancy.

The next platform is the near-term test. Nvidia’s Vera Rubin racks enter mass-production preparation this quarter and ship in the fourth, and Chiang expects it to become Foxconn’s major product next year.

The share that is shrinking

Here is the part the headline profit hides. Foxconn is winning a bigger market and losing position inside it.

Morgan Stanley expects its high-end rack market share to fall to 39% this year, from 51% in 2025, according to the Wall Street Journal. Analysts put that down to buyers seeking alternative suppliers rather than to any drop in output.

That diversification is visible everywhere. Microsoft is ordering hundreds of thousands of its own chips from TSMC, and every hyperscaler is doing some version of the same thing.

Analysts have a second worry. As AI server designs standardise, the hardware risks becoming a commodity, which lowers the barrier for rival assemblers.

Chiang rejected that reading outright. Standardisation, he said, “highlights the advantages of suppliers with scaled delivery and complete vertical integration”.

Record revenue, thinner margin

The margin line is the quiet counterweight. Gross margin was 6.12%, down 0.21 percentage points on a year earlier.

Operating margin did improve, to 3.75%, up 0.60 points. Net margin sat at 2.37%, slightly below last year.

So the mix has changed but the economics have not. Assembling servers is still a business measured in single-digit gross margins, and volume is what pays for it.

That is why the capacity plan is so large. Foxconn is expanding to hundreds of sites across 24 countries, close to double its earlier footprint, with new capacity in California, Texas, Wisconsin and Ohio.

The ceiling nobody at Foxconn controls

Chiang named the real constraint on 2027, and it is not demand. It is CoWoS, the advanced packaging technology from TSMC that AI chips depend on.

The market expects that capacity to grow by more than 50% next year. How much of it turns into rack shipments, Chiang said, “will depend on chip supply”.

Foxconn does not control that supply. Neither does Nvidia, which is why the bottleneck keeps moving up the chain rather than disappearing.

The iPhone half of the business has its own geography problem. Most iPhones are still assembled in China, though the bulk of those sold in America are now made in India.

The market is not applauding

Investors have seen these numbers and shrugged. Foxconn shares are up 17% this year, against a 57% gain for the broader Taiwan index.

The doubt is not about this quarter. It is about who pays for the next one, and Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon have now committed close to $2.4 trillion to AI over the coming years.

Some of that is borrowed. Alphabet sold $25bn of bonds to help fund its build, and Nvidia has assembled a $500bn package with Wall Street to finance customers who cannot pay upfront.

A tech rout in July was the market rehearsing that worry. One Federal Reserve official has asked whether AI is becoming too big to fail.

Foxconn has answered the only question it can. It has proved the demand is real, that it can build to meet it, and that doing so has quietly turned an iPhone company into an AI infrastructure company. What it cannot prove is that the people writing the cheques will keep writing them.

利润随之而来。 净利润达到新台币 599.7 亿元，约合 18.6 亿美元，同比增长 35%，为公司第二季度历史最高水平。

季度数字

合并销售额达新台币2.53万亿元，同比增长41%，环比增长19%。 利润和收入均超出分析师预期。

云和网络份额快速攀升。 据台湾中央通讯社报道，第一季度这一比例为 48%，其中计算占 15%，电子元件占 5%。

每股收益为新台币 4.27 元，去年同期为新台币 3.19 元。 上半年盈利达新台币1,098.9亿元，增长27%。

七月的规模更大。 据彭博社报道，当月收入跃升 54.2%，达到创纪录的新台币 9,465 亿元。

公司承诺什么

轮值首席执行官迈克尔·蒋(Michael Jiang)将这一转变视为结构性而非周期性的。 他对分析师表示，云投资“将成为鸿海未来几年最重要的增长动力”。

他提出了一个对于合同制造商来说很重要的区别。 与消费电子产品不同，人工智能基础设施的需求是稳定的，消费电子产品的生死存亡取决于季节周期。

他还辩称，扩建工作才刚刚开始。 到目前为止，云提供商和人工智能实验室是大买家，而用他的话说，政府和企业的采用仍处于起步阶段。

下一个平台是近期测试。 Nvidia的Vera Rubin机架本季度进入量产准备，第四季度出货，蒋预计它将成为富士康明年的主要产品。

份额正在萎缩

这是标题利润隐藏的部分。 富士康正在赢得更大的市场，但却失去了在其中的地位。

据《华尔街日报》报道，摩根士丹利预计今年其高端机架市场份额将从 2025 年的 51% 降至 39%。 分析师将其归因于买家寻找替代供应商，而不是产量下降。

这种多元化随处可见。 微软正在从台积电订购数十万个自己的芯片，每个超大规模厂商都在做同样事情的某个版本。

分析师还有第二个担忧。 随着人工智能服务器设计标准化，硬件有可能成为商品，这降低了竞争对手组装商的壁垒。

蒋断然拒绝了这一解读。 他表示，标准化“凸显了供应商规模化交付和完整垂直整合的优势”。

收入创历史新高，利润率下降

边缘线是安静的配重。 毛利率为6.12%，较上年同期下降0.21个百分点。

营业利润率确实有所改善，达到 3.75%，上升 0.60 个百分点。 净利润率为2.37%，略低于去年。

因此，组合发生了变化，但经济状况没有变化。 组装服务器仍然是一项以个位数毛利率衡量的业务，而数量才是它的代价。

这就是容量计划如此之大的原因。 富士康正在向 24 个国家的数百个工厂扩张，其足迹几乎是之前的两倍，在加利福尼亚州、德克萨斯州、威斯康星州和俄亥俄州新增了产能。

富士康无人控制的天花板

蒋指出2027年的真正限制，并不是需求。 AI芯片所依赖的就是CoWoS，台积电的先进封装技术。

市场预计明年产能将增长50%以上。 蒋说，其中有多少转化为机架出货量“将取决于芯片供应”。

富士康并不控制该供应。 英伟达也没有，这就是为什么瓶颈不断向上移动而不是消失的原因。

iPhone 业务的一半也有其自身的地理问题。 大多数 iPhone 仍然在中国组装，但在美国销售的大部分 iPhone 现在是在印度制造的。

市场并不买账

投资者看到这些数字后耸了耸肩。 富士康股价今年上涨了 17%，而台湾综合指数则上涨了 57%。

疑问不在于本季度。 问题在于谁为下一个人工智能买单，Alphabet、Meta、微软和亚马逊现已承诺在未来几年内向人工智能领域投入近 2.4 万亿美元。

其中一些是借来的。 Alphabet 出售了 250 亿美元的债券来为其建设提供资金，而 Nvidia 则与华尔街制定了 5000 亿美元的一揽子计划，为无法预付款的客户提供融资。

七月份的科技股暴跌让市场再次演练了这种担忧。 一位美联储官员询问人工智能是否已经变得太大而不能倒闭。

富士康已经回答了它能回答的唯一问题。 它证明了需求是真实的，它可以通过构建来满足需求，并且这样做已经悄悄地将一家 iPhone 公司转变为一家人工智能基础设施公司。 它无法证明的是，写支票的人会继续写支票。
